neighbours.label: Words of exuberant merriment and hearty laughter, mostly in literary narration (mirth, uproarious, merriment, irrepressible giggles); sober or sad words in the same frames stay quiet
fire: The whole tavern shook with boisterous mirth when the fiddler fell.
Old Tom told his jests amid peals of merriment and clapping.
A gale of hilarity swept through the village hall that night.
The children dissolved into uncontrollable giggles at the sight.
She threw back her head in a burst of jovial laughter.
The bridal feast was a scene of revelry and good cheer.
He answered with such rollicking humour that the guests howled.
Their irrepressible glee rang down the corridor all evening.
quiet: The whole tavern fell into a solemn silence when the fiddler died.
Old Tom told his troubles amid sighs of sorrow and regret.
A wave of dread swept through the village hall that night.
The children sank into exhausted sleep at the end of the day.
She lowered her head in a moment of quiet prayer.
The funeral feast was a scene of mourning and bitter tears.
He answered with such careful detail that the guests took notes.
Their weary footsteps sounded down the corridor all evening.
